subject: Dedicated GPU SKU policy & packing plan for LumenScale pilot
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenscale.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@lumenscale.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:13:00 -0500
Subject: Pilot sizing + constraints (RFP attached)

Ben —

Thanks for the PRD template yesterday. Attaching the RFP and an initial ops spreadsheet. High level: we plan to pilot Redwood Dedicated for a fraud-detection feature embedded in our mobile app.

Key constraints:
- Peak concurrent QPS estimate: 1200 TPS to start, 2k expected in month 2.
- Typical request: 1.2k token context (user history + prompt), responses ~200 tokens.
- Latency requirement: p95 < 1200ms for interactive flows.
- Data residency: US only; we can do a reserved pool.

Can you propose a SKU split (H100 / A100 / L4) and any packing/tiling approach? We care about cost efficiency but cannot sacrifice the 1.2s p95 requirement.

Attaching: LumenScale_RFP_2026-11-01.pdf and qps_and_profile_estimates.xlsx

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform Ops
LumenScale

---
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenscale.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing + constraints (RFP attached)

Elaine —

Thanks for the detailed RFP and the QPS sheet. Quick summary up front: we recommend a hybrid pool with primary L4 capacity for baseline throughput and H100 slots for long-context, high-memory bursts. A100 can be used as a fallback for predictable reserved throughput if you want a single architecture for long-running sessions.

Proposed starter mix (pilot):
- L4 (burstable commodity): 55% of slots — for short requests and heavy packing (good tokens/$).
- H100 (memory/dense long-context): 35% of slots — for the 1.2k token requests and pinned sessions.
- A100 (stable throughput, lower mem than H100): 10% of slots — used for predictable reserved capacity and fallthrough when H100 is constrained.

Rationale in one line: L4 gives the best unit economics at scale when we can pack many small inferences; H100 is necessary to keep p95 latency within 1.2s for long-context because of larger VRAM and better kernel mix for attention; A100 is a cost-effective mid-point but is less memory-friendly than H100 for worst-case sessions.

Irene, copying you to add packing/tiling specifics and KV-cache recommendations.

Next steps: 1) Irene to validate packing %s and expected p95 at current qps, 2) we schedule a pilot sizing sync this week, 3) if we agree, we’ll produce a trial commitment estimate.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Elaine Park <elaine@lumenscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing + constraints (RFP attached)

Elaine, Ben —

I dug into the qps profile and ran a quick sim with our pilot harness (attached results summarized inline). Key technical recommendations:

1) Packing strategy
- Use aggressive intra-request packing on L4 for stateless short calls (batch size targets 32–64 depending on token distribution). This reduces per-token kernel overhead and lowers cost by ~30% vs single-shot.
- For long-context (>=800 tokens), avoid cross-request co-packing with short requests on the same GPU because KV cache churn increases latency variance. Pin long-context sessions to H100.

2) KV cache and memory pooling
- H100 pool must be configured with 40–60% of memory reserved for pinned caches for your user-session pattern. This prevents eviction storms during peak.

3) Tiling/slotting policy (how we assign requests to hardware)
- Priority routing: pinned long-context -> H100; stateless bulk -> L4; falling back -> A100.
- Autoscale: L4 autoscale threshold at 65% utilization to keep headroom for spikes; H100 autoscale threshold at 80% because we expect fewer but larger sessions.

4) Expected latency (sim results)
- Stat sections (packed L4): p95 ~ 650–900ms at 1200 TPS equivalent (depends on packing efficiency).
- Pinned long-context (H100): p95 ~ 900–1100ms for 1.2k token in/200 out at 1:1 KV hit rates.
- Fallthrough to A100: p95 ~ 1.1–1.4s (worse at higher concurrency).

Notes and caveats: real-world KV hit rates will swing numbers; if your user sessions have poor reuse, H100 memory pressure increases and p95 will degrade.

I’m attaching a short runbook and a CSV with simulated latency curves. If you want, we can run a short baseline with a 48-hour traffic replay from your ops team.

—
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
(irene@redwood.ai)

Attachments: redwood-sku-reco-deck.pptx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenscale.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:17:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing + constraints (RFP attached)

Elaine —

From a commercial perspective, two notes:
1) If LumenScale is comfortable with a 6–12 month reserved commitment we can reduce unit costs on H100 by ~18% and on L4 by ~12% in the pilot quote. That would let us bias the pilot to more H100 headroom without a large cost delta.
2) We can structure a small performance SLT (service-level target) that guarantees p95 tail and triggers temporary credit return if we miss the target during the pilot.

Proposed immediate deliverables:
- Pilot quote with two variants: conservative cost (our earlier % mix) and latency-first (H100 bumped by 10–15 points, corresponding cost delta).
- Draft mutual action plan (timeline, KPIs, test dataset, success criteria).

Ben / Irene — can you produce the variant cost numbers by EOD Friday? Elaine — can you share the 48-hour replay if you want us to run the baseline?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
